newsitem.title: UK: Barclays down after HSBC comment.
newsitem.headline: Barclays down after HSBC comment.

text.p: Shares in Barclays Plc dropped on Monday after analysts at HSBC James Capel pointed out the bank's stock had risen sharply in recent months and National Westminster Bank Plc looked better value in the short term, market sources said.
Barclays was down 6-1/2p at 996 by 1043 GMT while NatWest was up 2-1/2p at 665-1/2.
"They are just saying there may not be much to go for in Barclays in the short term," said one source, "and that NatWest is slightly better value."
Separately, analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett also repeated their positive stance on NatWest following an update with the company on Friday.

"NatWest has announced 10,000 job cuts in the UK and that hasn't really excited the market yet," said Hoare Govett analyst Peter Toeman. "We feel that the market isn't really giving enough attention to the restructuring of the (NatWest) UK retail bank."
Capel analysts were also said to have raised some concerns about prospects at Barclays' investment banking unit, BZW, but said any shortfall would be made up elsewhere in the group.

The Capel comments came after year-end briefings with five of the six leading UK banks, sources said. The brokerage remains positive on the sector, preferring Lloyds TSB Plc and HSBC Holdings Plc as well as Barclays. Analysts at Capel were not immediately available for comment.

Toeman said BZW, in common with other investment banks, had experienced a tough second half of 1996 after a strong first half of the year, and that this might be coming to the fore after the sharp rise in Barclays stock in recent months.
Barclays shares were trading at just over 800p at the end of July.
